proof_summary: For each prime \(p\), valuation counting gives the numerator contribution \(\sum_{i\ge1}\lfloor n/p^i\rfloor^2\) and the denominator contribution \(\sum_{i\ge1}\sum_{k=1}^{M_i} k\lfloor M_i/k\rfloor\), where \(M_i=\lfloor n/p^i\rfloor\). The inequality \(\sum_{k=1}^M k\lfloor M/k\rfloor\le M^2\) is an equality exactly for \(M\le2\), so the quotient has positive \(p\)-adic valuation exactly when some \(M_i\ge3\), equivalently \(M_1\ge3\), which yields the stated threshold.
